subject: Admin Trail Evidence — export slices, timezone normalization, and HMAC manifests
messages:
From: Jenny Park <jenny.park@medicosys.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: security@medicosys.com
Date: Tue, 3 Aug 2027 09:14:00 -07:00
Subject: Request: admin-event export slice for audit

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the quick sync this morning. As a follow-up from our SOC 2 readiness checklist, our auditors (AuditOps) have asked us for a timebound extract of Redwood admin activity for July 2027. They want: 

- All admin events (role changes, API key creation/rotation, user invites, console logins, delegation changes, model deploy/rollbacks) between 2027-07-01 and 2027-07-31 UTC
- Events normalized to UTC with original-timezone preserved in a separate column
- Per-event HMACs for chain-of-custody verification, plus a manifest listing file checksums and HMACs
- Redaction guidance for user_email / ip_address fields (we can share a redaction policy)

Can you confirm:
1) What fields are present in the admin-event ledger export (schema)?
2) Export formats supported (NDJSON, CSV, Parquet)?
3) Delivery options (S3 presigned, SFTP, encrypted Drive link, or transfer via Secure FTP to AuditOps)?
4) Whether you can provide HMACs and the algorithm used (we need SHA256-HMAC or equivalent for our chain-of-custody).

We'd like a sample manifest and an example 24-hour slice so AuditOps can validate ingestion before the full bundle.

Thanks,
Jenny Park
Head of Security Programs
MedicoSys

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: Jenny Park <jenny.park@medicosys.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 3 Aug 2027 12:01:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Request: admin-event export slice for audit

Jenny — thanks for the clear ask. Short answers up front: yes, we can produce the slice with timezone-normalized timestamps, generate per-event HMACs, and deliver via S3 presigned or SFTP. Below I outline the schema and options; attaching a sample 24h slice and a manifest CSV in the next message.

Schema (default fields included in admin_activity export):
- event_id (UUID)
- occurred_at_utc (RFC3339 UTC)
- occurred_at_local (RFC3339 w/ timezone)
- actor_user_id
- actor_email
- actor_role_before
- actor_role_after
- target_resource_type
- target_resource_id
- action_type (API_KEY_CREATE, API_KEY_REVOKE, LOGIN_SUCCESS, LOGIN_FAILURE, ROLE_ASSIGN, MODEL_DEPLOY, MODEL_ROLLBACK, etc.)
- action_details (JSON blob)
- source_ip (redacted per policy)
- request_user_agent
- request_id
- kv_cache_delta (when applicable)
- hmac_sha256_hex

Retention notes: hot store (90 days) in primary telemetry; archived bundles are retained for enterprise customers per contract (default 2 years cold). If you require longer retention, we can add a retention override in the Dedicated/Private contract.

Export formats: NDJSON (recommended), CSV (flattened), Parquet (columnar, best for large ingests).

Delivery options:
- S3 presigned multipart download (AES-256 encrypted objects, KMS-managed)
- SFTP push to your security SFTP endpoint (AES-256 in transit + at-rest on endpoint)
- Encrypted bundle on Google Drive (shared link, client-managed key)
- Direct Transfer to AuditOps (we can coordinate a one-time SFTP url)

HMAC details: we support event-level HMAC using HMAC-SHA256 over a canonicalized concatenation: event_id + occurred_at_utc + actor_user_id + action_type + target_resource_id. We will provide manifest-hmacs.csv with lines: file_name, file_sha256, manifest_hmac (signed by Redwood key id). The manifest will itself be HMAC-signed using an ephemeral key; we can share the public verification key or deliver the key through your KMS.

Redaction: we can apply field-level redaction prior to export. For PII (actor_email, source_ip) we can either redact to tokenized ids or provide salted hash values. If you prefer reversible redaction, we require an escrow agreement and key handling plan.

I'll attach a 24-hour NDJSON sample and the manifest with HMACs in the next message for AuditOps to validate ingestion.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of Security Integrations | Redwood Inference

From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
To: Jenny Park <jenny.park@medicosys.com>, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.ai, olga_petrov@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 3 Aug 2027 12:27:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Request: admin-event export slice for audit

Jenny — attaching the sample bundle and manifest (small slice: 2027-07-15T00:00:00Z — 2027-07-15T23:59:59Z). Notes in the manifest:

- Files: admin_activity_slice_20270715.ndjson (NDJSON, gzip), admin_activity_slice_20270715.ndjson.sha256, manifest-hmacs.csv
- Each event line includes occurred_at_utc and occurred_at_local. We normalized to UTC for occurred_at_utc and left occurred_at_local as provided by the service.
- HMACs were generated with HMAC-SHA256 using an ephemeral Redwood signing key (key id: rwd-ephem-20270803). The manifest includes the manifest_hmac field and sha256 checksums for each archive file.
- Redaction: source_ip has been salted and hashed (sha256 hex) to support correlation without showing raw IPs. actor_email is partially redacted (first initial + domain).

[Attachment: admin_activity_slice_202707.zip (contains NDJSON + checksums)]
[Attachment: manifest-hmacs.csv]

Let us know if AuditOps needs the public portion of rwd-ephem-20270803; we can either publish it to your secure Drive link or share via your KMS envelope.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Senior Product Security Manager | Redwood Inference

From: Glenn Murray <glenn.murray@auditops.com>
To: Jenny Park <jenny.park@medicosys.com>, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 3 Aug 2027 16:11:00 +00:00
Subject: Re: Request: admin-event export slice for audit

Laura/Jenny — received the sample and started an ingestion test. A couple of requests from our side:

1) Can Redwood include an event_serial integer (monotonic per-file) to help reordering during parallel ingestion?
2) For redacted fields, please include the redaction_method column (e.g., SALTED_SHA256:base64salt). That helps us map back to test vectors.
3) We'll need the public key for rwd-ephem-20270803 to validate the manifest HMACs. Please put the pubkey on the Drive link you mentioned.

Otherwise the sample looks good — NDJSON schema validated and hashes match. We'll sign off once we validate the HMACs and reingest a 7-day slice.

—Glenn
Lead Auditor, AuditOps

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: Jenny Park <jenny.park@medicosys.com>, Glenn Murray <glenn.murray@auditops.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai, olga_petrov@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 4 Aug 2027 10:03:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Request: admin-event export slice for audit

Thanks, Glenn — we'll add the event_serial field and the redaction_method metadata. Action items: 

- Laura: upload rwd-ephem-20270803.pub to the Drive folder and add it to the manifest.
- Marcus: prepare a 7-day NDJSON bundle (2027-07-10 — 2027-07-16) and run manifest HMACs using rwd-ephem-20270803.
- Olga: coordinate SFTP handshake with AuditOps if they prefer direct transfer.

Delivery plan options (pick one):
A) S3 presigned bundle + manifest (we upload to your bucket path and issue presigned urls valid for 7 days)
B) Push to AuditOps SFTP endpoint (we can rotate the transfer credentials after upload)
C) Encrypted Drive bundle with client-managed key (Drive link + access ACL)

If MedicoSys prefers option A, we'll need a target bucket path and whether you want objects encrypted with Redwood KMS or your external KMS.

I'll follow up once Laura and Marcus confirm the files are staged.

—Karthik
Head of Security Integrations | Redwood Inference
